import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`ffi/env` tells whether the [FFI extension](https://www.php.net/manual/en/book.ffi.php)
can be used in the current runtime. It reads the state of `ext-ffi` and of the
`ffi.enable` directive and turns it into a status, a boolean or an exception with a
message that explains what is wrong.

## Installation

```bash
composer require ffi/env
```

Requires PHP 7.4 or later. The package does not need `ext-ffi` itself: its whole
point is to work when the extension is missing.

<Aside type="note">
The package supports PHP 7.4, the examples on this page use the syntax of the
current PHP version.
</Aside>

## Status

`FFI\Env\Runtime::getStatus()` returns one of the `FFI\Env\Status` constants:

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Status::NOT_AVAILABLE` | `0` | `ext-ffi` is not loaded. |
| `Status::DISABLED` | `1` | The extension is loaded, but `ffi.enable` is off: `0`, `false` or any other value that is neither a true boolean nor `preload`. |
| `Status::ENABLED` | `2` | The extension is enabled in every SAPI: `ffi.enable=1` (`true`, `on`, `yes` and non-zero numbers count as well). |
| `Status::CLI_ENABLED` | `3` | `ffi.enable=preload`: the FFI API works in the `cli` SAPI and in preload scripts only. This is the default value of the directive. |

```php
use FFI\Env\Runtime;
use FFI\Env\Status;

echo match (Runtime::getStatus()) {
    Status::NOT_AVAILABLE => 'ext-ffi is not loaded',
    Status::DISABLED => 'ext-ffi is disabled',
    Status::ENABLED => 'ext-ffi is enabled',
    Status::CLI_ENABLED => 'ext-ffi is enabled in CLI and preload only',
} . "\n";

// php -d ffi.enable=preload example.php
// ext-ffi is enabled in CLI and preload only
```

## Checking availability

`Runtime::isAvailable()` answers the question that usually matters: can FFI code
run here and now. It returns `true` for `Status::ENABLED`, and for
`Status::CLI_ENABLED` only when the current SAPI is `cli`.

```php
use FFI\Env\Runtime;

var_dump(Runtime::isAvailable());

// php -d ffi.enable=1 example.php  → bool(true)
// php -d ffi.enable=0 example.php  → bool(false)
```

<Aside type="caution">
Under `ffi.enable=preload` a web SAPI (FPM, Apache) is reported as unavailable even
inside a preload script: the package cannot tell a preload script from a regular
request.
</Aside>

Both methods accept a status as an argument, so a status read once can be reused:

```php
use FFI\Env\Runtime;

$status = Runtime::getStatus();

if (!Runtime::isAvailable($status)) {
    // ...
}
```

## Requiring FFI

`Runtime::assertAvailable()` returns `true` when FFI is available and throws
`FFI\Env\Exception\EnvironmentException` otherwise. The message explains the
reason, the exception code is the status.

```php
use FFI\Env\Exception\EnvironmentException;
use FFI\Env\Runtime;

try {
    Runtime::assertAvailable();
} catch (EnvironmentException $e) {
    echo $e->getMessage() . ' (code ' . $e->getCode() . ")\n";
}

// php -d ffi.enable=0 example.php
// An [ext-ffi] disabled in your php.ini (code 1)
```

| Status | Message |
|---|---|
| `NOT_AVAILABLE` | `An [ext-ffi] not available` |
| `DISABLED` | `An [ext-ffi] disabled in your php.ini` |
| `CLI_ENABLED`, outside of `cli` | `An [ext-ffi] can only be run in "cli" mode, but the current mode is "<sapi>" does not meet required runtime parameters` |

`EnvironmentException` extends `DomainException`. The message for a status is also
available without throwing: `EnvironmentException::getErrorMessageFromStatus()`.

## Checking only in development

Since `assertAvailable()` returns `true`, it fits into `assert()`. With
`zend.assertions=-1`, the usual production setting, PHP does not compile the
assertion at all and the check costs nothing:

```php
use FFI\Env\Exception\EnvironmentException;
use FFI\Env\Runtime;

// Throws EnvironmentException when FFI is not available.
assert(Runtime::assertAvailable());

// Or throws AssertionError with the message of the status.
assert(
    Runtime::isAvailable(),
    EnvironmentException::getErrorMessageFromStatus(),
);
```
